pages.title: UNESCO : Building Peace through Education, Science and Culture, communication and information
pages.description: Learn more about UNESCO's role, vision and results. UNESCO is the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization. Our aim is to promote peace and security through international cooperation
pages.text: UNESCO : Building Peace through Education, Science and Culture, communication and information Skip to main content Help Us Improve Your UNESCO Website Experience close Search Search Quick links: AI Response to Crisis Key Challenges ©Ramon R/Shutterstock.com COP31: Protecting our water reserves As COP31 takes place in Antalya, Türkiye (9-20 November 2026) on the theme of water and ocean resilience, UNESCO advocates for integrated solutions combining science, education and Indigenous and local knowledge. With glaciers, ice and snow, which hold nearly 70% of the world’s freshwater, melting rapidly, UNESCO is also releasing a report on how AI shapes our understanding of climate change. Read more 80 years in the service of peace On 4 November 1946, UNESCO's Constitution entered into force. Eighty years ago, an organization was born from a simple conviction: that peace is built in the minds of women and men, through knowledge, dialogue and cooperation. Since then, UNESCO has set international standards, protected heritage, defended freedom of expression, supported education and put science at the service of humanity. Relive the voices and moments that shaped its history, alongside its 194 Member States. Read more © UNESCO Delivering for people in crisis Culture, education, science, and information are essential needs in times of turbulence and crisis. They are powerful drivers of social cohesion, resilience, and hope in a better future. UNESCO plays a vital role in safeguarding the social and cultural foundations that underpin stability, dignity, and recovery for communities affected by crises. By protecting these pillars, we help ensure that societies can rebuild not only infrastructure, but also trust, identity, and the collective capacity to move forward. Read more ©UNESCO Our impact in communities Discover how UNESCO drives change around the world. Dreaming of becoming a nurse: Opening doors to education in Cameroon From promise to practice: How teachers in Kenya are taking action for safer schools and healthier learners Expanding access to Nepal’s cultural heritage through open knowledge Talking walls Load more UNESCO in brief UNESCO is the United Nations organization that promotes cooperation in education, science, culture and communication to foster peace worldwide. The Organization provides key services for its Member States, setting global norms and standards, developing tools for international cooperation, producing knowledge for public policies and building global networks of sites and institutions inscribed on its lists. Discover Thumbnail play_arrow © UNESCO Our fields of expertise UNESCO uses education, science, culture, communication and information to foster mutual understanding and respect for our planet. Our strategic objectives UNESCO's strategy addresses global challenges with goals in education, the environment, social cohesion, and technology. Delivering in times of emergencies UNESCO supports communities affected by conflict and natural disasters, ensuring access to quality education and safeguarding cultural heritage. Building stronger multilateralism UNESCO stands on the frontline of international cooperation, in close coordination with sister agencies of the UN System. UNESCO lists and designations UNESCO sites connect the world and highlight the best of our shared humanity. 1273 World Heritage Sites 849 Intangible Cultural Heritage 797 Biosphere Reserves 241 Global Geoparks Magazine: The UNESCO Courier Is journalism old news? At a time when anyone can publish and share content, an abundance of information guarantees neither its quality nor its accuracy. While digital platforms amplify access to the public arena as well as to information , they can also undermine the conditions for independent journalism. In this disrupted landscape, a critical question arises: how can we preserve journalism that is based on verified facts, sound judgment, and the public interest?
